newsitem.title: USA: Indiana corn/soy ratings mixed after spotty rains.
newsitem.headline: Indiana corn/soy ratings mixed after spotty rains.

text.p: Corn and soybean conditions varied across the state after widely scattered showers missed some areas but hit others with up to six inches of rain, according to the Indiana Agricultural Statistics Service.

"Rainfall was widely varied, missing some areas while dumping up to six inches in others," the report said. "Many areas of the state are still in need of rain, as soil moisture conditions continue to decline."
Corn was rated 66 percent good to excellent, up from the previous week. Corn was silking on 40 percent of the acreage.
Soybeans were rated 65 percent good to excellent, down five points from the previous week. Fifteen percent of the crop was setting pods, ahead of the five-year average.
Winter wheat harvest was 89 percent complete, although rains disrupted progress in some areas.
Pasture was rated six percent excellent, 40 percent good, 38 percent fair, 12 percent poor and four percent very poor.

Topsoil moisture was rated eight percent very short, 23 percent short, 55 percent adequate and 14 percent surplus. Subsoil moisture was five percent very short, 24 percent short, 61 percent adequate and 10 percent surplus.
